questions.stem: A patient can see distant objects clearly but struggles to read a book at normal reading distance. The optician diagnoses long-sightedness (hyperopia). What is the underlying problem and how is it corrected?

options.text: The eyeball is too long; corrected with a concave lens
The eyeball is too short or the lens is too thin; corrected with a convex (converging) lens
The cornea is cloudy; corrected with laser surgery only
The retina is damaged; corrected with glasses

questions.explanation: In long-sightedness, the eyeball is too short or the lens cannot become thick enough, so light from near objects is focused behind the retina. A convex lens adds extra converging power, bending light rays inward so they focus on the retina correctly.

questions.stem: A teenager is diagnosed with short-sightedness (myopia). They can read a book easily but cannot see the whiteboard at school. Which type of lens would correct this problem?

options.text: A convex (converging) lens that bends light inward
A flat lens that does not alter the light path
A concave (diverging) lens that spreads light out before it enters the eye
A coloured lens that filters certain wavelengths of light

questions.explanation: In short-sightedness, the eyeball is too long or the lens is too powerful, causing distant objects to be focused in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the light slightly before it enters the eye, moving the focal point back onto the retina.

questions.stem: Laser eye surgery (LASIK) reshapes the cornea to correct vision. For a short-sighted patient, would the laser need to make the cornea flatter or more curved?

options.text: More curved, to increase the refractive power
Flatter, to reduce the refractive power so light focuses further back on the retina
Thicker, to add more refractive material
The same shape, but with a different colour

questions.explanation: In short-sightedness, light is focused in front of the retina because the eye is too powerful. Making the cornea flatter reduces its refractive power, so light converges further back, landing on the retina. This achieves the same effect as wearing concave glasses.

questions.stem: An elderly patient finds that they can no longer focus on close objects as easily as before. This age-related condition is called presbyopia. What causes it?

options.text: The eyeball grows longer with age
The lens loses elasticity with age and cannot become thick enough for near focus
The optic nerve deteriorates, reducing colour vision
The cornea becomes more curved, over-refracting light

questions.explanation: With age, the lens becomes stiffer and less elastic. When the ciliary muscles contract and suspensory ligaments slacken, the lens can no longer spring into a thick, rounded shape for near vision. This is why many older adults need reading glasses.

questions.stem: A student wears contact lenses instead of glasses. Both contact lenses and glasses correct the same eye defect. What is a key advantage of contact lenses over glasses for this student?

options.text: Contact lenses permanently cure the eye defect
Contact lenses sit directly on the cornea, providing a wider field of corrected vision and being less affected by physical activity
Contact lenses are safer because they cannot cause any eye infections
Contact lenses work by a completely different optical principle than glasses

questions.explanation: Contact lenses sit on the cornea and move with the eye, providing consistent corrected vision across the full field of view. They are practical for sports and physical activity. However, they carry risks such as eye infections if not cleaned properly, and they do not cure the defect.
